DIAGNOSIS READY: Congestive Heart Failure secondary to an Atrial Septal Defect.

The echocardiogram confirms a left-to-right shunt causing pulmonary congestion (rapid breathing), and the abdominal imaging shows liver enlargement due to this cardiac backup. The pitting edema is a classic sign of the heart's inability to pump effectively, leading to fluid retention in the lower extremities. Given the clear evidence of structural heart disease and resulting fluid overload, no further questioning or testing is required.
